title: Keep the scenario script picker inside its panel
observation: At 923px, opening Choose script focuses a search field in an overflowing table and shifts content behind the sidebar. DOM inspection measured the table at 1180px wide with its left edge at −291px. The operator loses the surrounding form.
recommendation: Contain horizontal scrolling within the picker, keep selection and search visible, and place focus without scrolling the outer workspace sideways.
acceptance: At 923px and 1440px, open the picker with mouse and keyboard, filter and choose a script, and return to the group. No labels disappear behind navigation; focus remains visible.
resolution: Implemented in the initial UX delivery; reviewed against the existing workflow and regression coverage. See IMPLEMENTATION.md.

title: Separate planned, allocated and measured load
observation: A Reserved run offers Start Test while displaying Current/Target 1/1 VU and Actual VU 1 alongside zero latency and errors. A historical failed snapshot labels telemetry Healthy and metrics Live Summary without clear historical context.
recommendation: Make metric presentation depend on lifecycle and sample availability. Label allocation separately; show Not started or No samples instead of successful-looking measurement zeros. Label historical samples with full timestamps.
acceptance: Reserved, queued, running, disconnected and terminal fixtures distinguish allocation from observed load. No-sample latency/error values are unavailable, and historical health cannot imply current live health.
resolution: Pre-start and zero/missing-request snapshots use explicit unavailable-sample states; historical telemetry is identified as captured evidence.

title: Carry evidence limitations into conclusions and exports
observation: The report has nine request records, unknown elapsed time and termination, and 1 peak VUser against 22 planned. Evidence separately reports critical telemetry gaps, yet Executive Top Risks says no significant error patterns were recorded. An 85% coverage score does not communicate the critical limitation.
recommendation: Promote insufficient-evidence and critical telemetry findings to Summary and exported Top Risks. Separate measured errors from confidence in the test. Avoid inferring customer impact from generic latency/error prose.
acceptance: For this run, Summary and export both identify sparse workload evidence and critical telemetry gaps. No-errors text is qualified. Unknown values read naturally, including replacing Unknown/s elapsed-run average.
resolution: Implemented in the initial UX delivery; reviewed against the existing workflow and regression coverage. See IMPLEMENTATION.md.

title: Qualify baseline comparisons before showing regression claims
observation: The selected baseline produces raw deltas including +1980ms p95 and −44 VUsers, while the current run has nine request records and 1 peak VUser. The view does not explain whether differing workload and sample populations support comparison.
recommendation: Show comparability checks for script/scenario revision, workload, duration, sample count and metric definition. Keep descriptive deltas available but mark an unmatched or unknown baseline as unsuitable for a confident regression conclusion.
acceptance: A mismatched-load baseline displays a prominent qualification next to deltas; unknown metadata remains unknown. A matched baseline receives a clear comparison summary using the same metric populations.
resolution: Checks known scenario/project/application/release/load/duration context, available script/scenario revisions, and selected-population sample counts; missing metadata remains unverified.

title: Make missing-archive recovery useful
observation: An older Failed run appears with archive Pending. Its result page loses name/reference/status and says this run is complete. View execution snapshot initially lands on an empty Archive Report panel. Diagnostics later shows a delayed-publication banner and live-style telemetry, but no failure cause on that panel.
recommendation: Preserve run identity through errors; distinguish publishing, delayed, unavailable and failed archive states when supported by backend evidence. Open a useful overview or failure-diagnostics fallback, with a concrete explanation when failure details cannot be recovered.
acceptance: Open the observed jms-rel-run from Results: identity and Failed status remain visible, recovery never lands on an empty archive panel, and unavailable failure details have explicit next actions. Do not imply publication is still progressing without evidence.
resolution: Preserves run identity and opens retained overview details; both execution retry banners and Command Center avoid unverified publication claims.

title: Count scripts, not expanded detail rows
observation: Expanding one script changes pagination from 27 to 28 while the All filter remains 27. The desktop reproduction shows All 27 and Showing 1–10 of 28 together.
recommendation: Paginate logical records and render expanded details within their parent record.
acceptance: Expanding or collapsing any number of rows leaves item totals, page boundaries and the set of scripts on a page unchanged.
resolution: Implemented in the initial UX delivery; reviewed against the existing workflow and regression coverage. See IMPLEMENTATION.md.

title: Normalize the import form and prioritize the source
observation: New script folder name is a native gray input at 1440px (360×20px) and stretches into a 128.5px-high block at 923px. Destination setup precedes file selection, and an Agentforce option appears in the generic OpenAPI flow.
recommendation: Use the shared themed input with constrained dimensions. Lead with source selection and detected format; reveal destination and format-specific options when relevant.
acceptance: Both tested widths show the same input treatment and usable label/field spacing. The source step is obvious; specialized options do not compete with generic OpenAPI import.
resolution: Implemented in the initial UX delivery; reviewed against the existing workflow and regression coverage. See IMPLEMENTATION.md.

title: Make Settings search find actual settings
observation: Find settings returns No settings match for theme although Dashboard Theme exists in Personal preferences.
recommendation: Index field names and common synonyms as well as section titles, and send results to the matching control.
acceptance: Theme, dark, word wrap, rows and motion resolve to their relevant controls when available to the current role; searching never exposes inaccessible admin settings.
resolution: Search synonyms resolve to focused, visible controls across guarded Settings and Access-owned route changes.

title: Make cross-links respect the current role
observation: In User preview, Monitoring → Controller settings leads to personal Appearance with no explanation or visible return-to-monitoring control. This is misleading navigation, not evidence of an authorization bypass.
recommendation: Hide irrelevant administrative links or offer a clear read-only explanation of who can manage the setting. Preserve the return path when a destination cannot be opened.
acceptance: A non-admin following the Monitoring link gets an honest destination or explanatory state and can return to Monitoring; an admin reaches Controller settings.
resolution: Implemented in the initial UX delivery; reviewed against the existing workflow and regression coverage. See IMPLEMENTATION.md.

title: Reduce page chrome and preserve essential actions
observation: The script library consumes roughly 600px before records at the narrow viewport. Create-script choices stack above the form; Dashboard dates/actions and editor action controls require horizontal scrolling. Access layers tabs, links, filters, a table and details.
recommendation: Use a compact shared page header, one primary action, collapsible secondary filters and responsive essential columns. Reuse the Results list’s successful narrow-width treatment. Keep row actions and identifying context visible.
acceptance: At 923px, users can identify and act on a recent run or script without horizontal page scrolling. A completed dashboard run has a clear results action. Core editing controls are visible while ancillary metadata remains available.
resolution: Implemented in the initial UX delivery; reviewed against the existing workflow and regression coverage. See IMPLEMENTATION.md.

title: Define one readiness vocabulary across authoring
observation: Checkout HTTP is Ready · 100 in the library, but the editor says validation evidence not yet, Debugged missing and approval readiness needs evidence. These may represent different checks, but their scopes are not obvious. A workload-source warning appears on Scripts before the source step.
recommendation: Name each readiness dimension consistently: static validity, debug evidence, approval and run-model validation. Explain what each enables and defer future-step requirements until relevant.
acceptance: The same script has compatible status labels in library and editor; no unqualified Ready implies missing execution evidence exists. Each warning has an actionable current-step destination.
resolution: Implemented in the initial UX delivery; reviewed against the existing workflow and regression coverage. See IMPLEMENTATION.md.

title: Reset wizard scroll and focus on step changes
observation: After advancing to Data, the viewport remains down near the model preview and disabled fields instead of the new step heading. Run Settings appears complete on initial arrival using defaults.
recommendation: Move focus to the new step heading and reset the intended content scroll container. Distinguish valid defaults from a step the user has reviewed.
acceptance: Next and Back consistently announce and reveal the step at both widths and via keyboard, without losing entered values. Step status wording does not imply explicit review of untouched defaults.
resolution: Implemented in the initial UX delivery; reviewed against the existing workflow and regression coverage. See IMPLEMENTATION.md.

title: Align creation entry points with their promised task
observation: Create script opens Use existing. An empty scenario library offers Copy existing first. New Test has a useful builder link, but shows lengthy downstream setup before a scenario exists. Model and copy terminology obscures whether an original is changed.
recommendation: Open the requested creation mode, use a clear first-test path, describe copy versus edit explicitly, and defer downstream configuration until prerequisites exist.
acceptance: A first-time operator can create a script, build a scenario and configure a run without choosing unavailable copy sources. Save, Save copy and configure-run actions describe their effects accurately.
resolution: Implemented in the initial UX delivery; reviewed against the existing workflow and regression coverage. See IMPLEMENTATION.md.

title: Disambiguate runs before opening them
observation: The run selector contains duplicate names with identical Reserved or Queued statuses and no reference or creation time.
recommendation: Include stable reference, relevant time and workspace context, with grouping by lifecycle where helpful.
acceptance: Each duplicate-named run is distinguishable in the selector and its identity matches the workspace opened afterward.
resolution: Implemented in the initial UX delivery; reviewed against the existing workflow and regression coverage. See IMPLEMENTATION.md.

title: Use one explicit scheduling time convention
observation: One-off scheduling defaults to America/New_York while recurring schedules default to UTC. Both expose time zones, but switching modes changes the assumption.
recommendation: Use the same documented user or workspace default in both flows. Show the next occurrences with their time zone and handle daylight-saving transitions explicitly.
acceptance: Switching one-off/recurring preserves the intended time zone. Previewed occurrences agree with stored schedules, including a daylight-saving boundary.
resolution: Implemented in the initial UX delivery; reviewed against the existing workflow and regression coverage. See IMPLEMENTATION.md.

title: Correct Access action semantics and simplify inspection
observation: The inspected user-row action cell is labelled Service account actions in the DOM. The dense table/detail arrangement also duplicates inspection/edit entry points.
recommendation: Correct entity-specific accessible names and consolidate the inspect/edit path without hiding identity or role context.
acceptance: Keyboard and screen-reader checks identify the selected user and action correctly. Focus enters and returns from the details panel predictably. User and service-account rows are not mislabelled.
resolution: User/service-account identity cells retain their actual names; Inspect focuses the user-specific heading and shared collapse controls restore focus to Expand.

title: Make operator help easy to find
observation: User Guide and Quick Start live under API Guide, whose default page foregrounds REST response codes and development headers.
recommendation: Use Help & documentation as the entry, prioritize operator tasks, and retain API reference as a clear destination.
acceptance: An operator can find first-test, failed-run and report-interpretation help without recognizing API terminology.
resolution: Implemented in the initial UX delivery; reviewed against the existing workflow and regression coverage. See IMPLEMENTATION.md.

title: Make repository scope an explicit mode
observation: Repository explains that its domain/project/release filters are independent of the sidebar workspace. This is honest but requires operators to track two scope systems.
recommendation: Offer an obvious Current workspace / All accessible workspaces mode, with visible scope near results and explicit destination when opening an asset.
acceptance: A user can predict which assets will appear and whether opening one changes workspace; global browsing remains possible. Do not infer a permissions problem from different catalog totals.
resolution: Implemented in the initial UX delivery; reviewed against the existing workflow and regression coverage. See IMPLEMENTATION.md.
